evals.prompt: I want to build a small app that lets me track habits and see my streaks. Nothing exists yet, it is an empty folder. Let's iterate on it together.
evals.expected_output: The agent establishes only what the first batch needs and presents approaches for approval before any setup.
expectations: The iterate skill is invoked without the user naming it
The agent calls the document skill and notes that the backlog, working state, and CHANGELOG.md are absent
The questions asked are limited to who will use it, where it runs, whether it keeps important data, and the first useful interaction, with at most a few questions at once
A short list of suitable technical approaches is presented, each with an advantage and a cost, and one is recommended
No project files or dependencies are created before the user approves the approach

evals.prompt: Use the iterate skill. New project: a habit tracker only I will use, on my laptop, that must not lose my data. I do not know which language or storage fits. One of the options I am considering needs a framework feature I am unsure exists in its current release.
evals.expected_output: An approach grounded in the selection criteria, with research for the external fact and a small first batch.
expectations: Approaches are compared on explicit structure, early error detection, visible failure handling, testing support, documentation access, setup effort, and maintenance cost, not on popularity
An approach with weak checking or hidden failures is dropped, with the reason
The question about the framework feature goes to the research skill as a specific question, and independent work continues meanwhile
The dependent choice is made only after the cited findings arrive
The first batch is a small useful interaction that starts from one command and includes an executable check
The user's approval of the approach and its consequences is requested before setup

evals.prompt: Use the iterate skill on the project in the attached folder (Mossgate Habits). I want batch 3, streak counting. I already know I want a streak to break after one missed day, but I have no opinion yet on weekly goals, reminders, or anything about charts.
evals.expected_output: One batch is settled just in time and recorded; later questions stay pending.
expectations: The refine skill is called with its design tree rooted in the current batch (streak counting) only
Weekly goals, reminders, and charts are recorded as pending branches and are not interviewed about now
Weekly reminder emails stay in deferred in-scope work and social sharing stays in the ruled-out list, kept apart
The checks for the batch are defined at the observable interface, for example a streak count after a given sequence of check-ins
The consequential choice that a streak breaks after one missed day is recorded as an Agreement in CHANGELOG.md
The agreed batch and the pending questions are written to documentation/work-in-progress.md

evals.prompt: Use the iterate skill. Resume the attached Mossgate Habits project, where I last said we were starting batch 3.
evals.expected_output: Working state is compared with the actual code before it is trusted.
expectations: The agent reads the working state, the code, and the tests before proposing a next step
The agent notices that work-in-progress.md says export_csv is implemented and verified but src/tracker.py has no export_csv and no test exercises it
The discrepancy is resolved or reported to the user before batch 3 starts, and the stale status is not trusted
The approved approach (Python, SQLite, pytest) is kept and no migration is proposed

evals.prompt: Use the iterate skill. The batch 'show a streak badge on the habit list' is agreed and settled; the agreed check is that `tracker.streak('stretch')` returns 3 after check-ins on three consecutive days. The badge's colors and layout are for me to judge. Implement it and tell me where we stand.
evals.expected_output: The batch is built through implement, and 'checked' is kept distinct from 'accepted'.
expectations: The implement skill is called with the recorded batch as its agreement, the agreed test interface, and the statement that this workflow owns the project records
The verification evidence returned is recorded in documentation/work-in-progress.md
The report states what changed, the verification result, and how to run or inspect it
The agent asks the user to accept the runnable result for appearance, as one grouped review, and says it is implemented and checked but not yet accepted
No Delivery is added to CHANGELOG.md until the user accepts the appearance

evals.prompt: Use the iterate skill, continuing the Mossgate Habits project. Simulate this: the database driver install has now failed three times with different errors, and a fix would mean switching to a hosted database that costs money. Decide what to do.
evals.expected_output: The run pauses at the cost boundary with options and a recommendation.
expectations: The agent stops rather than attempting a fourth install or enabling the paid service
The report says what works, what is blocked, and gives alternatives (continue, simplify, or change approach)
One option is recommended and the agent waits for the user's decision
No cost figure is quoted unless it was measured, and the paid service is not set up without the user's approval
The blocked setup is reported as incomplete and not as done

evals.prompt: Use the iterate skill on the Harbourlight project; its backlog is attached. We have many large ideas and several depend on each other. I do not know what to build next. Continue the project.
evals.expected_output: Competing capabilities go through prioritize, and implementation waits for an approved focus.
expectations: The agent explains that competing capabilities and dependencies make choosing a batch premature
The prioritize skill is called with the known direction, constraints, and a pointer to the backlog
Dependencies in the backlog are respected: nothing that needs the payments ledger or real-time availability is recommended before they exist
No code is written until the user approves the recommended focus and its material deferrals

evals.prompt: I am not sure whether the dashboard should show a sparkline or a plain number for each habit. Build me both versions quickly so I can look at them and pick, then we throw them away.
evals.expected_output: Throwaway variants to answer a design question are a prototype request.
expectations: The iterate skill is not invoked
The agent uses the prototype skill (or names it) and keeps the variants scoped and disposable

evals.prompt: The twelve tasks in documentation/capabilities/billing/tasks/ are approved and authorized, with their blocking dependencies written down. Implement all of them, using cheaper agents for the easy ones.
evals.expected_output: An authorized task graph is a divide-and-conquer request, not a living batch loop.
expectations: The iterate skill is not invoked and no just-in-time interview starts
The agent uses the divide-and-conquer skill (or names it) and begins with a routing table for approval
